real_estate.homebuilder: Rates are unchanged at 6.89% because Mortgage News Daily did not publish on the holiday. The de-dollarization headlines that would push them higher do not survive a close read.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates are still 6.89% on the 30-year and 6.49% on the 15-year. Those are Friday's close and they have not moved since, because Mortgage News Daily does not publish on a federal holiday and Monday was Labor Day. The next real reading lands this afternoon.

There is a headline making the rounds that deserves a careful look, because it points straight at your mortgage rate. The dollar's share of global central bank reserves has fallen from 64% in 2015 to 56% in 2025. The worry writes itself: if the world stops parking money in dollars, it stops buying Treasuries, yields rise, and mortgage rates follow.

• The chart below is the actual research, from the New York Fed. Two things in it cut against the scary version. Roughly equal numbers of countries RAISED their dollar holdings as lowered them, and the entire aggregate decline traces to a handful of large holders, chiefly China and Russia, with Mexico and Morocco joining later. Among countries with complete data only Brazil and Hong Kong meaningfully cut.
• What that means in plain terms: this is a few big players rebalancing, not a world walking away from the dollar. It is not the thing that decides your rate this year. The August jobs report and the Fed's September meeting are.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Board wide: 2,620 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 235 coming soon and 124 brand new.
• Five city ledger: 695 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 588 are already on the market and 107 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 267 live, 208 active, 44 coming soon, 15 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,228,888 at $823 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 27 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 182, Milpitas 115, Newark 76, Union City 55.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,082,500 at $697 a square foot. 271 homes are priced under a million, and 155 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: inventory grew again over the long weekend, from 684 live listings yesterday to 695 today, and 74 of them arrived in the past week. More choice is genuinely good news for buyers who have been losing out. The pressure point is on the other side: 155 of the 588 homes on the market, better than one in four, have now been waiting two months or more. If your home is in that group, the issue is almost never the market. It is the price.

feature_image.alt: Line chart of the U.S. dollar share of global official foreign exchange reserves on a true time axis: 64% in 2015, 61% in 2019, 59% in 2023 and 56% in 2025, with the 2023 to 2025 segment falling 1.50 percentage points a year, twice the pace of earlier stretches.
feature_image.caption: Plotted on a true time axis, the recent decline is the steepest of the decade. But the same New York Fed research finds roughly equal numbers of countries raised as lowered their dollar holdings.
feature_image.source: Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Liberty Street Economics, "Are Central Banks Moving Out of Dollar Assets?", September 2, 2026. The 2019 and 2023 points are derived from the post's stated declines of 3 and 2 percentage points.

stocks.news:
Markets reopened this morning after the long weekend, so the levels above are Friday's closing bells rather than yesterday's. There was no Monday session to report.

As of 8:01 AM PT today the reopening is mixed to soft. The S&P is near 7,693, off about 0.34% from Friday's close, the Nasdaq is near 26,444, off about 0.24%, and the Dow is the weak one at roughly 52,854, down about 1.05%. Those are live intraday quotes and they will move before the closing bell.

Two items worth your attention. Google and Apple are both scouting Australia for AI data centers, drawn by clean power and proximity to Asia, with the country potentially attracting $107 billion of investment by 2030. And Uber is lining up its first ever euro denominated bond sale, joining nearly $145 billion of euro bonds sold by U.S. companies this year. Global corporate bond issuance has hit a record $4.9 trillion, most of it big tech funding AI.

economy.commentary:
China's central bank bought 650,000 troy ounces of gold in August, its biggest month in nearly three years and its 22nd consecutive month of buying, a streak that started in November 2024. Reserves are now at a record 76.73 million ounces, about 2,387 metric tons.

The chart below tells a better story than the raw headline does. China nearly stopped early this year, adding just 40,000 ounces in January and 30,000 in February. Then it bought more every single month after that, ending at 650,000 in August. That is more than a twenty fold acceleration inside eight months, and it is the sharpest signal in the data.

Why it matters beyond the metals desk: a central bank that buys gold every month for nearly two years is diversifying away from something, and gold near $4,477 an ounce reflects a lot of buyers reaching the same conclusion. It is also the same story as the dollar reserve chart in the Real Estate section above, seen from the other side.

Elsewhere, copper hit an all time high at $14,533 a ton in London, up about 47% from a year ago, as traders rushed metal into the United States ahead of possible tariffs. Copper sits in wiring, panels and plumbing, so that feeds directly into construction and renovation budgets.

A note on the newsletter's numbers, because three did not hold up. It quoted the 10-Year at 4.77% "as of September 7", but Monday was a federal holiday and Treasury published no yield curve at all that day. The last real reading is 4.78% from Friday. It also put Brent at $97.24 against the ICE front month settlement of $96.28, and gold at $4,469 on a holiday session that never settled.

feature_image.alt: Bar chart of troy ounces added to China's official gold reserves each month in 2026: January 40,000, February 30,000, March 160,000, April 260,000, May 320,000, June 480,000, July 640,000 and August 650,000.
feature_image.caption: China nearly stopped buying in February at 30,000 ounces, then added more every month through August. The January and February bars are missing from the version circulating today.
feature_image.source: Source: China State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), monthly change in official gold reserves. August was the 22nd consecutive month of buying and took reserves to a record 76.73 million ounces.

crypto.commentary:
These are live quotes pulled at 8:01 AM PT this morning with 24 hour changes, since crypto ran straight through the holiday. Bitcoin is soft near $78,500, Ether is close to flat, and XRP is the only one of the three in the green.

One newsletter claim needs correcting outright. Market Briefs reported that Bitcoin "went up 22.4% during the week ending September 4" and called it the best week since March 2024. Bitcoin closed that week at $79,824 against $78,246 the Thursday before, which is a gain of 2.0%, not 22.4%. The decimal appears to have wandered. The related claim that Bitcoin briefly crossed $82,000 is true: it touched $82,262 on September 2.

The real news is a security incident. Hackers took about $320 million from the Liquid Network, a Bitcoin sidechain several exchanges use to move coins, by exploiting how the network mints its wrapped version of Bitcoin. The network paused transactions in response. If you hold coins on an exchange that routes through it, expect slower transfers.
